title: The resolver line that came back empty
role: You are on call for a cloud platform's web proxies: a pair of nginx VMs (one active, one standby) in front of hosted projects. Puppet manages both.

source.label: Wikimedia: Incidents/2024-11-25 WMCS proxy nginx failure

brief: 03:12 UTC, you're paged: "Proxy on proxy-04 is down". proxy-04 is the standby; proxy-03 carries the traffic and looks fine.

steps.situation: The VM is up in the cloud console and SSH works. nginx is stopped and won't start again.
steps.evidence:
$ sudo systemctl restart nginx
Job for nginx.service failed because the control process exited with error code.
$ sudo nginx -t
nginx: [emerg] invalid number of arguments in "resolver" directive in /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/project-example:19
nginx: configuration file /etc/nginx/nginx.conf test failed

choices.text: Ask nginx what it dislikes: nginx -t and journalctl -u nginx
choices.why: It names the file, the line and the directive. Line 19 is a `resolver` line with no address in it.
nginx reads the same file after the reboot and fails the same way.

choices.text: Restart nginx a few more times
choices.why: A config error doesn't go away by retrying; systemd just records more failures.

steps.situation: Who wrote an empty resolver line? proxy-03 is built from the same Puppet code.

choices.text: Diff the config against the healthy twin, then check where the address comes from: /etc/resolv.conf
choices.why: This is how it was found at 03:54. proxy-04 has no nameserver line, and Puppet stripped the same address from the nginx files.

choices.text: Force a Puppet run: it will put the right config back
choices.why: It fails: Puppet can't resolve its own server, because the host has no nameserver. Useful only as a clue.

choices.text: Hand-type a public DNS server into the nginx file
choices.why: nginx starts, with a resolver nobody chose, and Puppet will overwrite it once it runs again.

steps.situation: Puppet itself fails with `Temporary failure in name resolution`. You recognise a known bug: Puppet sometimes removes the nameserver line from /etc/resolv.conf.

choices.text: Put the nameserver line back by hand, rerun Puppet, check nginx -t, start nginx
choices.why: What was done at 03:56. With DNS back, Puppet runs and rewrites the nginx files with the address, and both are fixed a minute later.

choices.text: Fix only the nginx file and go back to bed
choices.why: nginx runs, but the host still can't resolve names and Puppet stays broken until someone notices again.

choices.text: Disable Puppet on the proxies for good
choices.why: You trade one bug for two drifting servers that nobody manages.

steps.situation: 04:13, resolved. It was the standby, so no user saw anything; the alert cleared in Alertmanager but you had to close it by hand in the paging tool.

choices.text: Link the incident to the known bug, write a runbook for this alert, and review whether a standby proxy should page at night
choices.why: The report's actions. A runbook turns 40 minutes of searching into a checklist, and severity should match the impact.

choices.text: Silence all proxy alerts at night
choices.why: The next failure could be on the active proxy, with users watching.

choices.text: Nothing to do: no users were affected
choices.why: The bug is still there. Next time it may hit both proxies.

debrief.what_happened: At 03:09 UTC on 25 November 2024 Puppet removed the nameserver line from `/etc/resolv.conf` on the Cloud VPS proxy proxy-04 (a known bug, T379927) and also removed the nameserver address from its nginx site files, and nginx failed fatally. At 03:12 ProjectProxyMainProxyDown paged the on-call engineer, who found the VM up and SSH working, but nginx down and not restarting. At 03:54 the responder compared configs with proxy-03 and found the `resolver` line set there and empty on proxy-04. A forced Puppet run at 03:55 failed with a name-resolution error, which matched the known bug. At 03:56 the responder restored `/etc/resolv.conf` by hand and reran Puppet; Puppet and nginx were both fixed at 03:57. The alert cleared in Alertmanager but had to be resolved by hand in VictorOps; the incident closed at 04:13. There was no user impact, because proxy-04 was the standby. Actions: fix the Puppet bug, add a runbook for the alert and reconsider its severity.
lessons: Service won't start: nginx -t names the file and line.
Diff a broken host against its healthy twin.
Config management that renders from local facts breaks when the facts break.
Match paging severity to impact, and give every paging alert a runbook.
